top.headline: Trump Moves to End Biden-Era Methane Rule as Fuel Prices Become a Campaign Liability
top.blurb: Trump said his administration is terminating Biden-era limits on methane emissions from oil and gas drilling, framing it as a push for more domestic output as high fuel prices dog Republicans heading into next week's midterms. EPA chief Lee Zeldin had previewed scrapping the agency's 'Super Emitter Program' and loosening rules for small wells.

top.headline: Trump's Hunt for Noncitizen Voters Produced Almost No Cases — and Gutted Other DHS Investigations
top.blurb: Homeland Security Investigations ran state voter rolls through its databases at the administration's direction, despite its own lab warning of an 'ungodly' rate of false positives. From January 2025 to May 2026 the effort produced fewer than 150 referrals and 41 charges, while reassigning agents cut DHS wiretaps to 23 from 133 the year before.

top.headline: Gujarat Court Cites Vedas, Manusmriti While Sentencing Three Muslim Men to Life for Cow Slaughter
top.blurb: A Gandhinagar sessions court sentenced Wasim Kureshi, Mohammad Rafiq Kureshi and Asfak Bahelim to rigorous life imprisonment for slaughtering cattle, in a judgment whose opening pages invoke Hindu scripture — including the Manusmriti's description of the cow as the 'axis' of dharma — to justify the sentence. Police had seized about 277kg of beef from the men.

top.headline: Supreme Court Issues Notice to Election Commission and Gyanesh Kumar Over SIR Voter Deletions
top.blurb: The Supreme Court issued notices to the Election Commission and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on petitions challenging large-scale voter deletions during the special intensive revision, folding them into existing cases against the roll revision. Karnataka's SIR alone had already dropped nearly a crore of names from its final list.

more.headline: Rahul Gandhi, Nirmala Sitharaman Trade Accusations Over Tata Group's Troubles
more.blurb: Rahul Gandhi accused the government of damaging the Tata Group; Sitharaman accused Congress of inciting distrust, and he replied that businesses need no incitement to oppose the government.

top.headline: Trump Says He Approved Vance's Outreach to Iran as Tehran Presses Its Seven-Day Hormuz Plan
top.blurb: Trump said he approved Vice President JD Vance's outreach to Tehran over Iran's need for medical supplies but denied directing him to restart peace talks, while Iran's foreign minister said mediators remain in close contact over Tehran's seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The contact comes eight months into the war between the US, Israel and Iran, with no ceasefire yet in place.

top.headline: No Clear Winner in Israel's Election With Nearly 90 Percent of Votes Counted
top.blurb: Netanyahu's bloc is on course for 53 Knesset seats and Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc for 48, both short of the 61 needed to govern, while Arab parties are set for a record 19 seats that neither side will partner with. More than 500,000 special ballots are still to be counted, after the highest turnout since 1999.

top.headline: Brazilian Political Drama Unfolds as Defeated Flávio Bolsonaro Arrives in Miami
top.blurb: Flávio Bolsonaro landed in Florida days after losing Brazil's presidential runoff to Lula by more than four million votes, after Brazil's Supreme Court ordered him to surrender his passports over a money-laundering probe he denies. Lula called the departure 'shameful'; the US said it would issue visas letting him and his family stay.

top.headline: 'Fatherland' Review: A Gorgeous, Almost Flawless Film About Thomas Mann's Return to Germany
top.blurb: NPR's critic calls this black-and-white film about Thomas Mann's 1949 return to a defeated Germany gorgeous and nearly flawless, saying it doesn't waste a single second. The film follows the exiled Nobel laureate as he confronts a country, and a literary legacy, transformed by the war he spent it opposing from afar.

bengal.headline: BJP Factional Clash in Sitalkuchi Leaves Minority Morcha Leader Injured
bengal.blurb: A clash between rival BJP factions in Sitalkuchi's Baro Moricha left Minority Morcha district secretary Rezzak Hossain hospitalised after what his wife called an ambush at a 'mediation meeting'; the local Shakti Pramukh denies it, and both sides plan police complaints.

bengal.headline: Malda Medical College Launches Cardiology, Nephrology OPDs
bengal.blurb: Malda Medical College and Hospital opened new outpatient departments for cardiology and nephrology, giving district patients specialist care they previously had to travel to Kolkata to get.

travel.headline: Lonely Planet's Fall Travel Trends: 15 Places the World Is Going Next
travel.blurb: Booking data puts Japan atop this autumn's fastest-rising destinations for its Kyoto and Tokyo foliage, with Thailand, Vietnam, Sri Lanka and New York City also climbing the list.

travel.headline: Australian State Approves National Koala Park Despite Controversial Carbon-Credit Funding
travel.blurb: New South Wales passed legislation creating the 475,000-hectare Great Koala National Park to protect roughly 12,000 koalas, though critics warn its funding, drawn mainly from carbon credits, risks turning conservation into a commercial offset product.

happy.headline: Ivan the Terrible Wanted to Marry Elizabeth I. How Did England's 'Virgin Queen' Say No Without Losing the Trade?
happy.blurb: Drawing on a new biography, this traces how Ivan the Terrible's 1570 marriage proposal to Elizabeth I curdled into insults when she stalled, and how she rebuffed him so deftly that England's lucrative Muscovy trade carried on regardless.

tech_top.headline: Google Opens Gemini and Search to More Apps as AI Agents Reshape the Web
tech_top.pm_note: If AI assistants become the storefront, product visibility shifts from SEO toward being a registered 'connected app' inside Gemini and Search — a new distribution surface to plan for.
tech_top.blurb: Google launched a Connected Apps Platform that lets any developer link their service to Gemini and Search, so users can take actions — building a Canva flyer, queuing a YouTube Music playlist — without leaving the AI experience. More than 50 apps are already live in Gemini, with Search integrations rolling out over coming weeks.

tech_top.headline: Microsoft Disclosed $10 Billion in Quarterly Revenue From OpenAI
tech_top.pm_note: Two companies can compete for the same customers while remaining this financially entangled — a reminder that AI-platform 'coopetition' is now a quantified dependency, not just a talking point.
tech_top.blurb: A regulatory filing shows Microsoft earned $10 billion from its commercial arrangements with OpenAI last quarter, about 11% of Microsoft's total revenue, putting the relationship on a roughly $40 billion annual run rate even as the two increasingly compete for the same cloud customers. Microsoft's ownership stake in OpenAI has meanwhile slipped to 24%, from 27% a year ago.

tech_more.headline: Amazon Debuts the Alexa Photo Frame and Echo Time Smart Clock
tech_more.blurb: Amazon's new $199 Alexa Photo Frame uses Alexa+ to pick which photos to display, and its $199 Echo Time alarm clock offers sleep-phase-aware wake-ups, part of a broader Echo hardware refresh.

tech_101.text: An open standard that lets an AI assistant discover and call a third-party app's functions directly, rather than just reading its website. It's the plumbing behind Google's new Connected Apps Platform letting Gemini act inside Canva or YouTube Music on a user's behalf.

science.headline: A 60-Year Search Is Over: Chemists Isolate Long-Elusive Molecules With Boron-Oxygen Triple Bonds
science.blurb: Chemists at the University of Würzburg, working with Tezpur University in India, stabilized oxoboranes — compounds built around a boron-oxygen triple bond — at room temperature for hours at a time. It closes a question that had resisted chemists for six decades, since such bonds had only ever been glimpsed under extreme, fleeting conditions.

science.headline: NASA's Artemis I Mission Reveals Surprising Radiation Levels Near the Moon
science.blurb: Detectors riding in instrumented mannequins aboard the uncrewed Artemis I capsule found that cosmic radiation near the Moon runs higher than in low Earth orbit, though by less than some researchers feared. NASA says the data will shape shielding and storm-shelter planning for the crewed Artemis II and III missions.

philosophy.headline: We Need a Language to Name the Grief That Comes Without Death
philosophy.blurb: Philosopher Derek van Zoonen argues grief isn't only a response to death — a fading friendship, a changed identity, a childlessness never chosen also disrupt a life's possibilities. Because these 'ambiguous losses' carry no ritual or shared vocabulary, he argues, people struggle to name them, or to be seen in them by others.

philosophy.headline: Why a World Without Friction Is a World Without Progress
philosophy.blurb: Tribologist Jennifer Vail argues that friction, usually treated as a nuisance, has driven progress from the wheel to regenerative braking to dark-matter detection. Each advance creates new resistance in turn, she argues, so a genuinely frictionless world would offer only ease, never real advancement.

philosophy.headline: The Need That Makes Humans Unique in the Age of AI
philosophy.blurb: Philosopher Pia Lauritzen argues what distinguishes humans isn't some fixed trait AI might eventually match, but an ongoing need to define and redefine ourselves. That reframes 'what makes us human' as a question we keep answering, she argues, rather than one AI could ever settle for us.

philosophy_101.text: The study of friction, wear and lubrication between surfaces in contact — the science behind today's essay treating resistance as something to understand rather than eliminate.

A term from family therapy for a loss with no clear end point or ritual, such as a relationship that fades or an identity that changes, which today's essay on grief borrows to describe losses that aren't about death.
